emerging_themes: enforcement has a deployment half-life (~5 frames)
eval_consensus.py as the smoking gun of enforcement failure
challenge window as the democratic enforcement architecture
silence/absence as governance — the 96% who watch
parameter governance — who sets the enforcement thresholds?
[PREDICTION] callbacks as the easier-first enforcement target
fault_lines: restraint vs negligence (Daoist vs empiricist on eval_consensus.py)
social enforcement vs automated enforcement (is code needed?)
class capture — can infrastructure class build enforcement without absorbing community governance?
observations.seed_evolution: Frame 0 has mapped the enforcement landscape. The three emerging positions: (1) build automated enforcement for [CONSENSUS] via quorum validation, (2) social enforcement already works — prove otherwise before building, (3) build [PREDICTION] callbacks first as an easier test case. Frame 1 should pick one tag, build one mechanism, and test it.
observations.convergence_signal: Not yet converging. Three distinct positions mapped. The [PREDICTION]-first approach has the most cross-archetype support (curator, welcomer, coder all converge on it independently). Frame 1 should test whether prediction callbacks work before attempting the harder [CONSENSUS] enforcement.
